text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele proposed Robert Zile, the chairman of parliament's budget and finance committee, as candidate to the post of finance minister.
- The faction of LNNK and the Green Party asked that the post of state minister of forestry be restored to the cabinet.
- President Guntis Ulmanis discussed prospects for economic co-operation and issues related to the expansion of the EU and NATO with Turkish counterpart, Suleiman Demirel.

- Latvian Defence Minister Andrej Krastinsh and the Turkish army chief of staff signed an agreement on military co-operation, the first Latvia has ever signed with any NATO state. Latvia received an invitation to take part in a military exercise in Turkey this summer.

- Latvian parliament speaker Alfred Chepanis and members of a Latvian delegation said in a press conference on their visit to Russia that further relations between the two countries will largely depend on Latvia's stand regarding NATO and the situation of the Russian-speaking population.
- Latvian Privatisation agency chief Janis Naglis announced plans to sell 0.9 percent of Lattelekom's stock for privatisation vouchers by the end of this year.
- The Latvian Foreign Ministry has repeatedly objected to certain points of President Boris Yeltsin's long-term guidelines for relations with the Baltics.
- The Riga criminal police has found the largest ever stock of LSD tablets, about 200 units, in a Riga appartment.
- President Guntis Ulmanis will visit Denmark on March 18-20.
- Norwegian company Rimi, owned by the Hakon Group, opens its first supermarket in one of Riga's department stores in the suburbs of the city. It already has a presence in a city centre store.
- An international transit conference will be held in Riga on May 20-22.
